formula: target ~ 0 + (1 | Round) + (1 | Judge), as a probit on a latent difference per round: the round effect's SD fixed at 1, the judge biases' variance fixed by the prior and a latent SD per judge
notes: analcatdata boxing1 (Simonoff 2003): the first Lewis-Holyfield fight (1999), 12 rounds on the scorecards of 3 official judges and 7 media (Official flags the official ones), target 1 for a round scored for Lewis, even rounds counted for Holyfield. Algranati, Cork and Lee (2000, CMU tech. report 732, sec. 3.2 and 4.2) fit logistic regressions with round and judge factors, then their final direct Bayesian model (sec. 3.3 and 4.3, after Johnson and Albert 1999): a latent difference per round y_i ~ N(0, 1), each judge's perception y_ij ~ N(y_i + b_j, sigma_j^2) with b_j ~ N(0, tau^2), tau fixed by the prior, and a round scored for the first fighter when y_ij > 0. Official is an unused usable column. Outside check: the paper's hierarchical model replaces the inferred judge intercept.

notes: Read help page (Vlagtwedde-Vlaardingen FEV1, van der Lende et al. 1981). Long form, 133 men, 1-7 FEV1 measures each over years 0 to 19; id = subject. The R code of Fitzmaurice, Laird and Ware (2011, sec. 6.5) fits gls(fev1 ~ smoker*time, correlation = corSymm(form = ~ year | id), weights = varIdent(form = ~ 1 | year)) and keeps this linear trend over the quadratic model2 by a likelihood-ratio test; the subject cluster of the marginal model is rendered as a random intercept (geepack ruling, m3#22), the covariance named in the formula. Knafl, Beeber and Schwartz (2012, Res Nurs Health 35) compare linear mixed models on these data, random intercept and slope models with a smoker + factor(time) mean among them (not read here, the publisher blocks scripts). Outside check: the book's model replaces the recalled random-slope model.

notes: Read help page (ACTG 193A AIDS trial; Henry et al. 1998). 1309 patients, 1-9 CD4 measures; id = patient, logcd4 = log(CD4 + 1) (raw not in table); group = 4 treatment arms (declared categorical). The R code of Fitzmaurice, Laird and Ware (2011, sec. 8.8) fits model1 = lme(logcd4 ~ week + week16 + trt.week + trt.week16, random = ~ week + week16 | id), week16 = (week - 16) * I(week >= 16) and trt = I(group == 4), triple therapy against the three dual ones, then model2, which adds age and sex; its SAS code fits the adjusted model with one treatment contrast, trt*(week16 - week). The hinge and the trt recode stay in the formula only; the fields keep group, week and their interaction. Outside check: the book's adjusted model replaces the recalled one.
